episodes.title: Surviving a Family Tragedy and Finding Hope in Recovery
episodes.description_html:
Welcome to the Living Louder Podcast, where raw honesty, resilience, and hope take center stage. In this powerful episode, we sit down with James Spillet—a young man whose life has been shaped by unimaginable tragedy, addiction, and ultimately, profound transformation. James’s story is a testament to the strength of the human spirit and the possibility of redemption, even after experiencing the darkest moments.

James opens up about his tumultuous childhood growing up in Utah, navigating a fractured family environment marked by addiction, emotional abuse, and the absence of a consistent father figure. From an early age, he was exposed to substances like huffing gasoline, marijuana, psychedelics, and prescription pills, which set him on a path of substance abuse that would span over a decade. His journey includes dealing drugs as a young teen, battling psychosis, and living through the devastating loss of his entire family—his father, two siblings, and stepbrother—who all tragically died in a family murder-suicide. James’s account of that night is both heartbreaking and inspiring, revealing how he managed to survive and find a way forward despite overwhelming grief.

Throughout the episode, James shares the struggles of addiction, the cycles of relapse, and the relentless pursuit of sobriety. He talks candidly about the ups and downs of his recovery journey—from multiple treatment centers, jail time, and solitary confinement, to finally embracing a life of honesty, faith, and self-improvement. His story highlights the importance of accountability, community support, and the power of persistence in overcoming addiction.

More than just a story of hardship, this conversation delves into themes of hope, healing, and the importance of seeking help. James emphasizes that no matter how bleak life may seem, there is always light on the other side of darkness. He encourages others who are struggling to reach out, ask for help, and believe in the possibility of living a fulfilling, meaningful life beyond addiction and trauma.

This episode is a reminder that resilience is born from adversity, and that even in our lowest moments, we can find the strength to rebuild. Whether you’re battling addiction, facing family trauma, or simply seeking inspiration, James’s story offers hope and a call to action: you are not alone, and your story is still being written.

Join us in listening to a story of heartbreak, hope, and healing. Be inspired by James’s journey of transformation and learn how he is now helping others find their way out of the darkness.

Welcome to the Living Louder podcast, where we believe that every story has the power to inspire, heal, and transform lives. In this episode, we dive deep into the extraordinary journeys of ordinary people—stories of resilience, faith, love, and redemption that will touch your heart and challenge your perspective.

Join us as we sit down with Jon Adams, a man whose life has been profoundly shaped by his family’s legacy in photography, faith, and service. From growing up in a close-knit, hardworking family in Utah to building his own life around the values of kindness, perseverance, and continuous learning, Jon shares insights about his childhood, his parents’ influence, and the lessons he learned from a life of service.

A significant part of our conversation revolves around the powerful lessons Jon learned from his parents and grandparents—particularly his grandfather, known as the legendary “Chicken Man,” who traveled from town to town capturing family memories with a camera that weighed more than most of us can lift! Jon recounts stories about his family’s work ethic, their faith, and how they prioritized relationships and service above all. These stories reveal the importance of loving others, making time for family, and investing in what truly matters.

But this episode goes beyond just family stories. We explore the incredible impact of service, especially in difficult circumstances. Portia shares her own profound experience of working in prisons, teaching about love and connection, and how genuine care can bring about miracles—like calming tense situations and even preventing violence. Her stories will inspire you to see the strength in vulnerability, the heroism in overcoming trauma, and the importance of extending kindness even in the most challenging environments.

We also discuss the importance of mental health, overcoming shame, and breaking societal stereotypes about those who have faced adversity, including incarceration. Both Portia and Jon emphasize that everyone is fighting battles unseen, and that compassion can change lives—sometimes in ways we least expect.

Whether you're interested in family legacy, faith, service, or personal growth, this episode offers meaningful insights and practical wisdom. It’s a reminder that our past, no matter how difficult, can shape us into stronger, more compassionate individuals. And that through love, service, and understanding, we can all make a difference—one act of kindness at a time.

Tune in for inspiring stories, heartfelt reflections, and a call to live louder—more intentionally, more compassionately, and more connected to those around us.

episodes.title: Prison and Rebirth - Betsy Gallegos
episodes.description_html:
Welcome to the Living Louder Podcast, where real stories of struggle, hope, and transformation come to life. In this episode, we sit down with Betsy Gallegos—a woman who has lived through the depths of addiction, incarceration, heartbreak, and ultimately, redemption. Her journey is a powerful testament to the resilience of the human spirit, the guiding hand of faith, and the transformative power of hope.

Betsy’s story begins in the beautiful islands of Hawaii and Tonga, where her cultural roots and early life shaped her worldview. Growing up in a strong LDS family, she describes her teenage years as joyful and full of faith—until the shadows of addiction crept in during her mid-20s. From her first drug experience at 24 to the devastating loss of her unborn child, Betsy’s life took a dark turn that led her into years of relapse, street life, and dangerous situations. Her tale is filled with raw honesty about the struggles of addiction and the feelings of hopelessness that often accompany it.

But her story doesn’t end there. After a series of arrests—including kidnapping charges and federal gun charges—Betsy found herself in county jail and eventually federal prison. Her first days behind bars were surreal, filled with spiritual experiences and moments of divine intervention that reminded her she was not alone. From meeting fellow inmates with incredible stories to moments of clarity during LDS services, Betsy’s faith was reignited in the most unexpected places.

Through hard work, faith, and a relentless desire to change, Betsy turned her life around. She completed treatment programs, went back to school, and now works in recovery and support services, helping others who are battling similar struggles. Her journey of forgiveness, healing, and rebuilding her relationships with her children is truly inspiring. Today, she is living proof that no matter how dark the night, the dawn of hope is always possible.

Join us as Betsy shares her story in her own words—an unfiltered account of addiction, incarceration, faith, and love. This episode is full of encouragement for anyone feeling lost or overwhelmed, reminding us all that transformation is possible and that our pasts do not define our futures.

Whether you’re on your own journey of recovery, seeking hope for a loved one, or simply looking for an inspiring story of resilience, this episode will leave you inspired, uplifted, and more hopeful than ever.

episodes.title: Vanessa’s Story of Survival, Loss, & Love. The Ultimate Comeback
episodes.description_html:
Podcast Description:

In this powerful and heartfelt episode of the Living Louder podcast, Vanessa MacNeill shares her raw, emotional, and inspiring journey through some of life's most difficult challenges. From a childhood marked by family trauma, addiction, and loss, to her courageous fight for sobriety and healing, Vanessa’s story is a testament to resilience, love, and the transformative power of hope.

Growing up in Utah and California, Vanessa experienced a tumultuous family life, including her father’s tragic death and her mother’s heartbreaking loss. She candidly discusses her early struggles with drug addiction, including her first encounter with methamphetamine at just 16 years old, and how her life spiraled into a series of tumultuous events, including incarceration, mental health battles, and losing loved ones to suicide. Despite all of this, Vanessa’s story isn’t one of despair—it’s a story of overcoming, of finding strength in vulnerability, and of discovering that healing is possible no matter how dark the past may seem.

Throughout the episode, Vanessa openly talks about her journey with addiction, mental health, and her path to recovery. She shares her experience of losing her father to suicide, her mother’s tragic death, and the impact of these losses on her life. Yet, amidst the pain, Vanessa emphasizes the importance of love, connection, and spirituality—finding beauty in the scars and using her story to inspire others who are struggling.

Vanessa’s story is not just about surviving; it’s about thriving and choosing to live louder than the pain. Her honesty about her past, combined with her unwavering hope for the future, makes this episode a must-listen for anyone looking for motivation, compassion, and a reminder that even in our darkest moments, there is a light waiting to be found.

Join us as Vanessa reflects on her journey of self-discovery, the importance of community and faith, and her vision of helping others through her work in recovery. Whether you’re battling addiction, grief, or simply seeking inspiration to turn your life around, Vanessa’s story will touch your heart and remind you that you are never alone in your struggles.

Tune in to this episode for a candid, empowering, and uplifting conversation about resilience, love, and the incredible strength of the human spirit.

Podcast Description:

In this powerful, raw, and inspiring episode, we sit down with Gabe, aka Gaby Omega, a talented performer, songwriter, and man in recovery. His story is a compelling journey through the highs and lows of life, marked by addiction, crime, loss, and ultimately, redemption. From growing up in Los Angeles with talented parents who worked in the entertainment industry, to experiencing the chaos of addiction and street life, Gabe’s story is a testament to the resilience of the human spirit and the transformative power of faith and sobriety.

Gabe shares candidly about his childhood, the influence of his family, and the restless spirit that fueled his early years. His journey into music was a sanctuary and a discipline, but beneath the surface, there was a restless discontent that led him down a dark path of alcohol, drugs, and criminal activity. His story takes us through his time in and out of jail, homelessness, and the dangerous street life that almost claimed his life. Despite these struggles, Gabe’s faith and the support of recovery communities helped him find a way out.

He talks openly about hitting rock bottom, the moment he realized he was spiritually sick, and how surrendering to God changed everything. His journey through multiple rehabs, facing the reality of his addiction, and making amends with those he hurt, exemplifies the power of humility, honesty, and spiritual growth. His story highlights that recovery is not just about abstaining but about reconnecting with what makes us human and finding joy in serving others.

Gabe’s story is also about second chances — how he rebuilt his life, reconnected with his passion for music, and now uses his talents to inspire others. He performs at recovery events, mentors youth, and works in treatment centers, sharing his experience to help others find hope and purpose. His message is clear: no matter how dark the night, there is a path forward, and it begins with humility, faith, and a willingness to change.

Join us as we explore the depths of addiction and recovery, the importance of spiritual connection, and the incredible journey of redemption. Whether you're in recovery, supporting a loved one, or simply seeking inspiration, Gabe’s story will remind you that no matter how lost you feel, there’s always hope for a new beginning.

episodes.description_html:
Podcast Description:

Welcome to the Living Louder podcast, where stories of resilience, hope, and transformation take center stage. In this powerful episode, we sit down with Estavan, a man whose life story is nothing short of extraordinary. From a young age, Estavan faced unimaginable hardships—growing up in a family surrounded by addiction, experiencing repeated incarceration, and surviving a near-fatal accident that changed his life forever. His journey is a testament to the human spirit's capacity for change and the profound impact of second chances.

Estavan’s story begins in Salt Lake City’s West Valley, where he was introduced to drugs at just 14 years old. His early years were marred by family struggles, substance abuse, and countless run-ins with the justice system—over 70 juvenile arrests and multiple prison stints. Despite these setbacks, Estavan’s determination to break free from the cycle of addiction and violence kept him pushing forward. His narrative takes us through harrowing moments, including a life-threatening incident where he jumped from a moving van at 75 miles per hour, leaving him with a traumatic brain injury and a long road to recovery.

Throughout the conversation, Estavan shares the raw realities of living in toxic relationships, the challenges of navigating a system that often feels stacked against him, and the powerful moments that sparked his desire to change. His story also highlights the importance of community, family, and the role that organizations like Suntech Concrete have played in his transformation. Suntech’s commitment to seeing potential in their employees, providing second chances, and fostering a family-like culture allowed Estavan to turn his life around. Today, he is not only a safety professional dedicated to keeping others safe but also a living example of how perseverance and support can lead to a better future.

This episode explores themes of redemption, the significance of employment in recovery, and the importance of community and brotherhood. Estavan’s journey shows that no matter how dark the past, there is always hope for a brighter future—one built on hard work, humility, and faith. His story is an inspiration to anyone feeling trapped in their circumstances, reminding us all that change is possible when given the right support and opportunity.

Join us for this heartfelt conversation that will challenge your perceptions, inspire your soul, and remind you of the incredible strength within us all to overcome life's toughest battles. Whether you’re on your own journey of healing or simply seeking motivation, Estavan’s story will leave you inspired and ready to face whatever comes next.

episodes.title: Breaking Free: How Tiffany Overcame a Life of Drugs, Violence, and Trauma
episodes.description_html:
Welcome to the Living Louder podcast, where real stories, raw honesty, and inspiring journeys take center stage. In this episode, we sit down with Tiffany Ingraham—a woman who has faced some of life’s darkest challenges and emerged stronger, wiser, and more resilient than ever. Tiffany’s story is a powerful testament to the transformative power of hope, faith, and perseverance.

Growing up in Utah, Tiffany’s childhood was filled with love, family bonds, and a strong connection to her grandma, who was her anchor. However, her early life was also marred by chaos, addiction, and neglect. Her mother, caught in a cycle of partying, drugs, and unstable relationships, left Tiffany feeling abandoned at just 14 years old. Despite these hardships, Tiffany’s connection to her grandma and her faith in God became guiding lights through her tumultuous journey.

Throughout her story, Tiffany shares her experiences with substance abuse—including alcohol, marijuana, cocaine, and methamphetamine—and how these substances were intertwined with the trauma, confusion, and pain she endured. From early experimentation at age 12, to criminal activity, jail time, and the heartbreaking reality of her children’s birth and struggles, she openly discusses her battles with addiction, her moments of despair, and her ultimate desire for healing.

What makes Tiffany’s story truly inspiring is her unwavering hope and her relentless pursuit of a better life. She talks about her journey to sobriety, the pivotal moments that shifted her mindset, and the importance of community, therapy, and faith in her recovery process. Tiffany’s honesty about her setbacks, relapses, and the ongoing work of self-discovery offers a powerful message for anyone facing their own struggles.

Today, Tiffany is a shining example of resilience. She’s been sober for nearly a year, actively working on her mental health, reconnecting with her children, and embracing her purpose. Her story highlights that no matter how dark life gets, there’s always a path to healing, growth, and second chances. Her message to others is simple but profound: “Go toward the light, make your decisions, and stick to them. Everyone deserves hope and the opportunity to change.”

Join us for an emotionally charged, authentic conversation that will inspire you to reflect on your own journey, find hope amidst hardship, and recognize the power you hold within to transform your life. Tiffany’s story is a reminder that even in the midst of chaos, healing is possible—and it starts with a single choice.

episodes.title: From the Streets to the Feds. Fighting for Change
episodes.description_html:
Welcome to the Living Ladder podcast, where we dive deep into stories of redemption, resilience, and transformation. In this powerful episode, we sit down with Aaron Pila, an ex-felon who has lived the harsh realities of the federal prison system and come out on the other side with a mission to change lives. Aaron’s journey is nothing short of inspiring—he’s gone from living a street life filled with crime, drugs, and loyalty to becoming a voice for change, advocating for prisoners and shedding light on the systemic issues within the incarceration system.

Aaron shares raw and honest stories about his early years, his time in prison, and the struggles he faced while fighting legal battles that threatened to keep him behind bars for decades. You’ll hear about the brutal realities of high-security prison environments like Victorville USP, the underground networks that influence the streets, and the mental and emotional toll of incarceration. Despite these hardships, Aaron found purpose in helping others and using his voice to advocate for reform.

Throughout our conversation, Aaron emphasizes the importance of humanizing those in prison, breaking stigmas, and recognizing the strength and potential of every individual behind bars. He talks about the loyalty and connections formed in prison, the underground economies, and how the system is designed more for control than rehabilitation. His journey of faith, self-discovery, and relentless pursuit of purpose is a testament to the power of perseverance.

Aaron now dedicates his life to inspiring others, sharing his story through social media, and working with nonprofits to bring awareness to the injustices faced by incarcerated individuals. He’s also involved in efforts to influence policy change and supports programs aimed at rehabilitation and second chances. His story reminds us all that no matter how dark the past, there is always hope for a brighter future.

This episode is a must-watch for anyone interested in criminal justice reform, personal growth, or stories of overcoming adversity. Aaron’s transparency about his experiences offers a unique perspective on the prison system, loyalty, and the human capacity for change. If you’re ready to be inspired and learn what’s really happening behind prison walls, tune in now.

episodes.title: Fighting for Equal Opportunities - Steve Solen
episodes.description_html: Welcome to the Living Louder podcast, where authentic conversations about education, personal growth, and overcoming life's challenges take center stage. Hosted by Portia Lauder, this inspiring series features candid interviews with educators, leaders, and everyday heroes who are making a difference in their communities and beyond.In this episode, we sit down with Steve Solon, the passionate and innovative principal of Pleasant Creek School, a unique alternative school dedicated to serving at-risk youth, including those from group homes and juvenile detention centers. Steve shares his remarkable journey from growing up in Utah with strict religious parents to becoming a leader in education who believes in teaching kids to think critically, own their mistakes, and pursue success on their own terms. His story is a testament to resilience, authenticity, and the power of caring leadership.Throughout our conversation, Steve delves into his childhood in Orem, Utah, and discusses how his experiences with strict upbringing and cultural expectations shaped his approach to education and life. He emphasizes the importance of building trust with students and fostering genuine relationships—key elements that help kids open up and thrive, especially those who have experienced trauma or rejection elsewhere. Steve’s approach is rooted in empathy, transparency, and a commitment to teaching life skills that prepare students for real-world success.He also talks about the evolution of his career—from being a PE teacher and coach to navigating the challenges of working in traditional and charter schools, and eventually leading Pleasant Creek School. Steve highlights the importance of innovation in education, advocating for personalized learning, hands-on skill development, and creating an environment where students feel cared for and understood. His insights into funding disparities and the need for more equitable resources for rural and alternative schools shed light on systemic issues that hinder educational opportunities.Moreover, Steve openly shares the story of his tattoos, breaking stereotypes about appearance and faith, and illustrating how authenticity and self-expression can coexist with religious beliefs. His stance on mental health, trauma-informed care, and the importance of showing kids they are valued resonate deeply throughout the episode.This episode is a heartfelt reminder that education is not a one-size-fits-all system but a personalized journey that requires genuine care, innovative thinking, and courageous leadership. Whether you're an educator, parent, or someone passionate about making a difference, this conversation offers valuable lessons on authenticity, perseverance, and the transformative power of caring leadership in education.Join us as we explore how educators like Steve Solon are changing lives, one student at a time, and discover how we can all contribute to creating a more compassionate and effective educational system.#LivingLouder #EducationReform #AlternativeSchool #TraumaInformed #Leadership #SchoolInnovation #RuralEducation #AtRiskYouth #PersonalGrowth #AuthenticLeadership #EmpathyInEducation #CommunityImpact #SchoolTransformation

episodes.title: A Child of the Street Abandoned & Rescued
episodes.description_html: Welcome to the Living Louder podcast, where stories of resilience, faith, and hope come to life. In this inspiring episode, we sit down with Abby Viveiros, a woman whose life journey is nothing short of miraculous. From being found as a street child in Korea to becoming a loving mother and advocate for healing and redemption, Abby’s story is a testament to the power of faith, forgiveness, and the human spirit.Abby’s childhood was shaped by hardship and uncertainty. Found abandoned on the streets of Korea at just two years old, she faced a life filled with uncertainty, trauma, and cultural upheaval. She shares vivid memories of her early years—being cared for by strangers, navigating orphanages, and experiencing moments of innocence amidst chaos. Despite these challenges, Abby’s story is one of incredible resilience. She describes her journey from orphanage to adoption, her struggles with attachment and trust, and how she found hope and healing through her relationship with God.In this heartfelt conversation, Abby opens up about her transition to life in America, her feelings of loneliness, and her determination to find meaning and purpose despite her difficult beginnings. She discusses her experience with faith, how she turned to Jesus Christ for healing, and her ongoing journey of forgiveness—both for herself and those who hurt her. Her story highlights the importance of compassion, understanding, and recognizing the goodness in others, even in the most broken circumstances.Abby also reflects on her time in prison, sharing how she found a deeper connection to God during her darkest days. Her story underscores that transformation is possible for everyone, regardless of their past. She emphasizes the importance of choosing to see potential in others, offering grace, and extending kindness—principles she lives by today.This episode is a powerful reminder that every life has a story worth sharing, and that hope and love can emerge from even the most difficult trials. Whether you’re dealing with trauma, seeking faith, or simply looking for inspiration, Abby’s story will touch your heart and renew your faith in the goodness of humanity.Join us for this meaningful conversation and discover how faith, compassion, and resilience can transform lives. episodes.title: From Feral to Fighter: Anne Coburn’s Journey Through Addiction and Redemption
episodes.description_html:
In this compelling episode of the Living Louder podcast, we sit down with Ann Coburn—a woman who has traversed the darkest valleys of addiction, incarceration, and childhood trauma, and emerged into a life dedicated to hope, service, and transformation. Ann’s story is a raw, honest, and inspiring account of her journey from a feral, invisible kid to a passionate advocate for those most overlooked by society.

Growing up in Utah with older parents and a severely mentally ill mother, Ann faced a childhood filled with instability, neglect, and a deep sense of not belonging. Her early years were marked by rebelliousness, gang involvement, substance abuse, and a series of life-altering moments—including losing her father at age 14. Despite her turbulent past, Ann’s resilience shines through as she shares how she eventually found her way into the Odyssey House treatment program, a pioneering therapeutic community that helped her confront her demons and begin the healing process.

Ann’s journey through Odyssey was transformative. She describes the intense, peer-driven environment that taught her accountability, self-awareness, and the importance of community. Her story underscores the power of belief—believing in others even when they don’t believe in themselves—and how that belief can be a catalyst for change. Her candid reflections on her past mistakes, her struggles with mental health, and her ongoing process of growth offer valuable insights into the realities faced by those caught in the cycle of addiction and incarceration.

After years of sobriety and service, Ann took her passion for helping others to new heights. She now works in the criminal justice system and runs a nonprofit dedicated to supporting individuals transitioning from prison back into society. She emphasizes the importance of community, connection, and second chances, advocating for more compassion and understanding in systems that often marginalize the most vulnerable.

This episode is a must-listen for anyone interested in criminal justice reform, addiction recovery, or personal transformation. Ann’s story reminds us that everyone has potential—regardless of their past—and that with the right support, belief, and love, people can turn their lives around in remarkable ways.

Join us for an authentic conversation filled with hope, honesty, and inspiration. Whether you’re a professional working in social services, a person in recovery, or simply curious about the human capacity for change, Ann’s story will resonate deeply and encourage you to look at others with compassion and understanding.

episodes.description_html:

Welcome to an extraordinary episode that dives deep into the fascinating and often dark world of crime, deception, and redemption. In this episode, we sit down with Matt Cox, a notorious con artist whose life story reads like a Hollywood thriller. From humble beginnings marked by struggles with dyslexia and a challenging childhood, Matt’s journey takes us through the high-stakes world of mortgage fraud, identity theft, and elaborate scams that amassed millions of dollars and made national headlines.

Matt’s story is a rollercoaster of deception, risk, and ingenuity. He shares how his dyslexia, once seen as a debilitating obstacle, became a unique strength as he crafted complex schemes that fooled banks, lenders, and authorities alike. His ability to manipulate systems and create convincing fake documents led to a series of elaborate cons, including fake bank websites, fabricated corporate histories, and staged property transactions. Despite the danger and legal consequences, Matt describes the adrenaline rush and addictive nature of outsmarting the system, which kept him on the edge for years.

Throughout our conversation, Matt openly discusses his arrests, federal indictments, and the lengthy prison sentences that followed—26 years initially, later reduced through a series of legal appeals and cooperation efforts. He reveals the internal struggles, the moments of regret, and the ways prison life became a surprising source of clarity and transformation. His self-awareness about his addictive personality and his past choices offers a candid perspective on how he navigated a path filled with deception.

But this episode isn’t just about the crimes; it’s about the human side of a man who, despite his flaws, seeks redemption and a new purpose. Matt talks about his post-prison life, including how he’s built a new career as a podcaster, author, and speaker. He discusses the importance of honesty, the lessons learned from a life of crime, and the hard-earned wisdom that now guides his decisions. His story is a testament to resilience, showing that even in the darkest circumstances, change and growth are possible.

Join us for a raw, unfiltered conversation that explores the mind of a con artist turned storyteller. Whether you're interested in true crime, personal transformation, or understanding the complexities of human behavior, this episode offers valuable insights and a compelling narrative that will leave you thinking.

episodes.description_html:
Welcome to the Living Louder podcast, where raw, real stories of transformation, resilience, and hope are shared to inspire others to break free from their past and create a brighter future. In this powerful episode, we sit down with Dustin Blackner—a man who has lived through the harsh realities of gang life, addiction, and incarceration, and who has found a way to turn everything around. Dustin’s story is a testament to the fact that no matter how dark your past may seem, change is always possible when you decide to wake up and take control of your life.

Dustin’s childhood was filled with trauma, abuse, and exposure to violence. Growing up in a rough neighborhood in Utah, he was introduced to drugs at a very young age and became deeply entangled in gang life by his early teens. His story includes heartbreaking moments like witnessing a murder as a young boy and enduring years of mental, emotional, and physical abuse from his stepfather. Despite these challenges, Dustin managed to survive and navigate a cycle of incarceration, addiction, and hardship for over two decades.

But what makes Dustin’s journey truly inspiring is his unwavering desire to change. After numerous stints in prison, he reached a breaking point that sparked a profound internal shift. Through faith, community, and sheer determination, Dustin committed to sobriety and personal growth. Today, he’s been sober for nearly two years, actively working to rebuild his relationships with his family, especially his wife and children, and helping others do the same.

In this episode, Dustin shares candid insights into the realities of prison life—challenging stereotypes and revealing the brotherhood, humor, and even love that exists behind bars. He discusses the importance of discipline, self-love, and the power of choosing positivity even in the darkest moments. His story highlights that change is not only possible but inevitable when you take responsibility for your life and surround yourself with supportive, like-minded people.

Dustin also talks about the misconceptions often portrayed in media about prison and gang life, emphasizing that most inmates are just people trying to find their way, and that real strength comes from within. His message is clear: no matter where you come from or what mistakes you’ve made, you have the power to rewrite your story.

This episode is a must-watch for anyone seeking hope, motivation, or a reminder that true transformation starts from within. Dustin’s story proves that even in the face of adversity, love, faith, and perseverance can lead to a life of purpose and peace.

episodes.title: From Prison to Power: An Inspiring Journey of Redemption & Faith
episodes.description_html: Welcome to the Living Ladder podcast, where stories of transformation, faith, and resilience come to life. In this powerful episode, we sit down with Michael Germaine Mansfield — a man whose life journey is nothing short of extraordinary. From growing up with spiritual teachings as a child to battling addiction, experiencing homelessness, and ultimately finding redemption through faith—Michael’s story is a testament to the profound power of hope, repentance, and perseverance.Michael’s early years were deeply rooted in spiritual teachings, influenced by his father’s involvement in the I Am Activity and the teachings of Saint Germain. These teachings emphasized the divine nature within each of us and the power of the “I Am” consciousness. Despite this solid foundation, teenage years brought chaos—drugs, addiction, and the allure of a fast-paced, dangerous lifestyle. He was heavily influenced by the cartel, gang culture, and the destructive cycle of addiction that nearly cost him everything.Through harrowing experiences—selling drugs, gang stalking, and hitting rock bottom—Michael’s life seemed destined for despair. But his story takes a dramatic turn when he chooses to turn himself in and serve time in prison. It was in the prison cell that he found the truth in the scriptures, particularly the Book of Mormon, and recognized how the adversary had taken control of his life. His journey of faith, sobriety, and repentance began here, and today, Michael is a living example of radical change.After prison, Michael committed fully to his faith and sobriety. He went on to study at BYU Idaho, earning a degree in construction management, and now works as a traveling construction manager—living proof that no matter where you start, you can rise above your circumstances. His story is one of hope for those battling addiction, incarceration, or feeling lost in life. Michael believes that everyone can change, and his mission now is to inspire others to overcome their struggles and find their purpose through faith and hard work.In this episode, Michael shares intimate details about his childhood, the teachings that shaped him, the challenges he faced in his teenage years, and the lessons learned along the way. He talks openly about the importance of accountability, faith, and divine guidance in his transformation. His passion for politics, the war on drugs, and his desire to advocate for prison reentry and rehabilitation shine through. Most importantly, his story demonstrates that true happiness and strength come from within—and that everyone has the power to change their life for the better.Join us for an inspiring conversation that will uplift your spirit, renew your faith, and remind you that no matter how dark the night, the dawn of hope is always within reach. Whether you’re battling addiction, facing tough life circumstances, or simply seeking motivation to live your best life, Michael’s story will resonate deeply.Remember, your past does not define your future. The journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step. episodes.title: Heartbreak to Hope: Lily's Come Back - Lily Johansen
episodes.description_html:
In this powerful episode of the Living Louder Podcast, we sit down with Lily Johansson, a young woman who has endured unimaginable hardships and come out the other side stronger than ever. Lily’s story is a raw and honest journey through childhood trauma, mental health struggles, addiction, incarceration, near-death overdoses, and ultimately, redemption. Her resilience and determination to rebuild her life after years of chaos will inspire anyone facing their own battles.

Growing up in Davis County, Lily’s childhood was marred by an unstable family environment, physical and emotional abuse, and early diagnoses of PTSD, OCD, ADHD, and depression. Despite these challenges, she was a hardworking, dedicated individual with dreams of excelling in track and basketball. Tragically, the loss of her father to suicide and a series of substance use began to take over her life during her teenage years. She started experimenting with marijuana and alcohol before falling into deeper substance dependencies, including cocaine, Xanax, and bath salts, which led her into dangerous situations and multiple overdoses.

Lily’s story takes a dramatic turn when she overdoses in a drug house and is saved by Narcan, witnessing firsthand the deadly grip of addiction. Her journey through treatment, relapse, and recovery is filled with moments of despair, hope, and finally, success. Her experience with inpatient treatment, sober living, and the importance of support systems highlights the power of resilience and the human spirit to heal. Lily shares her insights on how unhealthy relationships, trauma, and addiction intertwine, and how she learned to break free from those cycles.

One of the most inspiring parts of her story is her realization that she can use her pain to help others. Lily now works in recovery, sharing her story at high schools and with those still struggling, showing that recovery is possible and that every step forward matters. Her message emphasizes the importance of working on oneself, healing family wounds, and never giving up—even when the road is long and difficult.

This episode is a testament to the transformative power of hope, perseverance, and faith. Lily’s journey reminds us all that no matter how dark life may seem, there is always a path to healing and a brighter future. Whether you’re battling addiction, trauma, or just need a little inspiration to keep going, Lily’s story will touch your heart and renew your faith in the possibility of change.

Join us as we explore the real, unfiltered truths of addiction and recovery, and learn how Lily’s faith, family, and inner strength helped her rebuild her life from the ground up. Don’t miss this empowering conversation—you’ll walk away inspired, uplifted, and ready to face your own challenges with renewed courage.

episodes.title: Prison lessons and Life Wins
episodes.description_html:
Welcome to the Living Louder podcast — a raw, inspiring conversation about resilience, redemption, and transformation. In this episode, we dive deep into the powerful stories of women who have experienced the realities of incarceration and emerged stronger, wiser, and more determined than ever. Join us as we share heartfelt insights about life behind bars, the struggles of rebuilding relationships, the importance of accountability, and the incredible opportunities for growth that come through programs like ARDAP and others.


Our guest, Meredith Fossey, generously shares her journey from growing up in Wyoming with LDS values, to a life of addiction and drug dealing, and ultimately to her time in federal prison. She talks openly about her experiences in various correctional facilities, the importance of education and therapy in prison, and how those experiences helped her find her true self. Meredith emphasizes that prison can be a place of healing if you’re willing to embrace the process and take accountability for your actions. She also reflects on her relationship with her kids, the challenges of reconnecting after incarceration, and the valuable lessons she learned about boundaries, self-worth, and personal growth.


Throughout this episode, we explore the significance of programs like ARDAP, which provide women with the tools and support needed to turn their lives around. We discuss how these programs foster accountability, teach life skills, and help individuals understand addiction from a professional perspective. Meredith and I also talk about the importance of community, the power of forgiveness, and the necessity of setting boundaries — both in prison and in life.


This conversation is not just about incarceration; it’s about hope, second chances, and the relentless human spirit. Whether you’ve experienced the system firsthand or are simply curious about stories of transformation, this episode offers valuable lessons on resilience, the importance of self-awareness, and the profound impact of taking responsibility for your life choices.


If you’re interested in stories of real people overcoming adversity, or if you’re looking for inspiration to make positive changes in your own life, this episode is for you. Tune in to hear candid, heartfelt stories that challenge perceptions, inspire growth, and remind us all that it’s never too late for a second chance.


Don’t forget to like, comment, and subscribe for more honest conversations about life, struggles, and triumphs. Share this episode with anyone who needs a reminder that redemption is possible, and that the journey to a better life begins with a single step.

episodes.title: Overcoming the Trauma of Prison and a Sex Offense
episodes.description_html:
Welcome to the Living Louder podcast, where we dive deep into stories of resilience, hope, and transformation. In this heartfelt episode, Portia and her daughter CJ share their extraordinary journey through some of life's most challenging moments — from incarceration and trauma to healing and growth. This honest and raw conversation offers a rare glimpse into the struggles faced by families affected by incarceration, sexual abuse, and mental health issues, all while highlighting the power of love, forgiveness, and resilience.


Portia opens up about her experience going to prison, the shock and pain of being separated from her children, and the emotional toll of facing a long sentence. She reflects on the difficulty of explaining her absence to her young children and the process of rebuilding trust and connection once she returned home. CJ shares her perspective as a young girl who was only seven when her mom was taken away, describing how she coped with the separation and navigated life in her mom’s absence. She honestly discusses the feelings of loneliness, confusion, and the moments where she felt she had to be strong for her family.


The conversation takes a powerful turn as CJ reveals her journey through trauma and abuse, and how therapy and open communication helped her find healing. She talks about the importance of honesty, vulnerability, and seeking support, emphasizing that healing is a process that takes time and courage. This episode also explores the impact of societal judgments, the importance of compassion, and how shared struggles can foster deeper understanding and connection.


Throughout the episode, Portia and CJ emphasize the significance of choosing love over bitterness, the importance of forgiving oneself and others, and the strength found in vulnerability. They discuss how their shared experiences have shaped their outlook on life, relationships, and the importance of mental health awareness. Both share inspiring messages of hope for anyone going through similar hardships, encouraging listeners to embrace their journey and focus on healing and self-growth.


Whether you're interested in stories of family resilience, mental health, overcoming trauma, or simply looking for an honest, inspiring conversation, this episode offers valuable insights and a reminder that even in the darkest times, there is hope and light. Join Portia and CJ as they share their truth, celebrate their progress, and inspire others to live louder, love deeper, and never give up.

https://www.cleanslateutah.org/

In this powerful episode of the Living Louder podcast, host Portia Louder sits down with Destiny Garcia, an inspiring advocate, community leader, and mother who has overcome incredible odds. From a childhood marked by violence, abuse, and trauma, Destiny shares her deeply personal story of addiction, homelessness, and the journey to recovery. She candidly discusses her experiences with abusive relationships, her struggles with opiate and meth addiction, and her time spent cycling in and out of jail. Despite these hardships, Destiny’s resilience and determination led her to find hope, purpose, and a new life through advocacy, education, and community support.


Destiny recounts the pivotal moments that transformed her life, including her participation in Operation Rio Grande, her efforts to seek treatment, and her eventual role as the executive director of Clean Slate Utah — a nonprofit dedicated to helping individuals clear their criminal records and rebuild their lives. She emphasizes the importance of sharing her story openly and loudly, not only to heal herself but to inspire others who feel trapped in the cycle of addiction, violence, or incarceration. Her journey from homelessness and addiction to working with local government and advocating for systemic change exemplifies the power of second chances.


Throughout this episode, Destiny talks about the importance of mental health, the impact of trauma, and the significance of community support and belief. She highlights how her life changed when people in her community, including the mayor of Salt Lake City, believed in her and gave her opportunities she never thought possible. Destiny’s story underscores that everyone deserves a chance at redemption and that honest, open conversations about addiction and recovery can foster understanding and change.


Join us as Destiny Garcia shares her heartfelt story, her advocacy work, and her hopes for the future. Whether you’re in recovery, supporting someone who is, or simply looking for inspiration to overcome your own struggles, this episode offers hope, encouragement, and a reminder that transformation is possible — no matter how deep the wounds.

episodes.description_html:
Welcome to the Living Louder podcast, where we dive deep into inspiring stories of resilience, love, service, and personal growth. In this episode, we are joined by the incredible Wilcox family—parents, grandparents, and grandchildren—who share candid, heartfelt conversations about their life's journey. From overcoming childhood traumas to navigating the challenges of Vietnam war, prison, loss, and family struggles, this episode is a testament to the power of perseverance and unconditional love.

Meet Cliff Wilcox, a Vietnam veteran who survived intense conflict, two Purple Hearts, and a series of health challenges including kidney failure and strokes. Cliff’s story is one of courage, determination, and transformation. Despite a tumultuous youth filled with risks and adventures, he turned his life around, embodying resilience and the spirit of a survivor. His reflections on his military service, the importance of choosing to be the best soldier he could be, and the value of having mentors who helped him through dark times serve as powerful lessons for all.

Portia’s mother, Chris, shares her story of motherhood, loss, and unwavering faith. Her childhood was filled with unique experiences, growing up in a free-spirited, no-rules environment that fostered creativity and independence. She recounts her journey of raising seven children in the country, providing them with a childhood full of adventures, outdoor fun, and life lessons. Her compassionate heart shines through as she discusses her love for children, her service to neighbors and community, and how her faith has helped her weather life's storms, including the heartbreaking loss of a child and her own struggles with addiction and healing.

Portia herself offers a powerful perspective on transformation, redemption, and the importance of working on oneself to influence positive change in others. She shares her personal journey of overcoming incarceration, battling addiction, and finding strength through faith and family. Her story underscores that it’s never too late to reinvent yourself and that hope and love can lead to profound healing.

Together, this family embodies the true meaning of living louder—embracing life’s challenges with compassion, humor, and resilience. Their stories are a source of inspiration for anyone facing difficult circumstances, reminding us that no matter how tough life gets, love, service, and perseverance can guide us toward a brighter future.

episodes.title: Resilience in the Face of Adversity: A Mother’s Story of Love and Forgiveness
episodes.description_html:
Episode Title: From Chaos to Clarity: A Mother’s Journey Through Addiction, Prison, and Redemption


Description:

In this heartfelt and honest episode of the Living Louder podcast, Portia and her daughter Shelby share their powerful story of resilience, love, and transformation. This episode takes you on a deep journey through a family’s struggles with addiction, the chaos of growing up in an unpredictable environment, and the path to healing and forgiveness.


Portia opens up about her tumultuous past, including her battles with addiction, her time in prison, and the profound lessons she learned through her experiences. She describes how her addiction began at a young age, how she navigated the legal system, and the traumatic experiences she faced during incarceration, including illegal treatment and the emotional toll it took. Despite these hardships, she emphasizes the importance of faith, accountability, and the power of God's grace in her recovery journey.


Shelby offers her perspective as her mother’s daughter, recounting her upbringing in a home filled with love but marked by a lack of structure. She shares how her childhood was filled with adventure, independence, and moments of chaos, but also how she developed a desire for stability and structure as she grew older. Shelby reflects on her own struggles with addiction avoidance, her admiration for her mother’s strength, and her feelings about her father’s love and adoption process.


Throughout the conversation, they discuss the impact of Portia’s incarceration on their family, how it changed their views of justice and compassion, and the importance of facing the truth. They also talk about the significance of boundaries, accountability, and forgiveness in fostering healing within their family.


This episode is a raw, emotional, and inspiring story of overcoming adversity, embracing vulnerability, and finding hope in the midst of hardship. Whether you're facing your own challenges or seeking insight into family dynamics, this conversation offers valuable lessons on love, resilience, and personal growth.


Join us as we explore these candid moments, and discover how love and faith can transform even the darkest experiences into opportunities for growth and redemption.


Tune in for a powerful story of hope, healing, and the strength of family.

episodes.description_html:
Welcome to a deeply honest and inspiring episode of the Living Louder podcast! Today, Chad and his spouse open up about their incredible journey through life's most difficult trials, sharing insights, struggles, and lessons learned along the way. From the chaos of addiction, the pain of legal battles, and the weight of incarceration, to rebuilding a marriage rooted in faith, forgiveness, and resilience — their story is a powerful reminder that no matter how hard life gets, we can find hope, purpose, and transformation.


In this episode, you’ll hear firsthand how Chad’s perspective on personal accountability and focusing on the “end game” helped them weather some of their darkest days. They talk about the importance of owning your part in any relationship or challenge, and how living by principles has been a guiding force through adversity. Their honest conversation covers the importance of emotional discipline, the power of forgiveness, and the strength it takes to choose love over anger—even when everything feels overwhelming.


They reflect on the early days of their marriage, the different worlds they came from, and how they navigated the adjustments and sacrifices necessary to build a life together. You’ll learn about the role of faith, prayer, and intentionality in healing wounds and fostering growth. Their story highlights that true change is possible at any stage of life, and that vulnerability and honesty are essential tools for personal and relational transformation.


This episode isn’t just about overcoming individual struggles — it’s about the power of community, support, and seeing the good in others, regardless of their past. They emphasize the importance of humanizing people who have made mistakes and the need for society to cheer on those who are working hard to rebuild their lives. From their experiences, they offer practical advice for couples facing challenges, as well as encouragement for anyone feeling stuck or overwhelmed.

episodes.title: Building Character Behind Bars - Ricky Zazueta
episodes.description_html:
Welcome to the Living Louder Podcast, where stories of resilience, transformation, and hope come to life. In this powerful episode, we sit down with Ricky Zazueta, also known as Smash, a man whose life journey is nothing short of extraordinary. From growing up in the rough neighborhoods of San Diego in a family with a history of gang involvement and incarceration, to turning his life around through faith, education, and relentless self-improvement, Ricky’s story is a testament to the power of inner strength and perseverance.


Throughout our conversation, Ricky shares candid insights about his early years, the struggles with addiction, and the dark places he found himself in. Despite these hardships, he made a conscious decision to change—learning to visualize success, build character, and embrace a new purpose. His dedication to personal growth is evident as he details his journey through prison, the importance of community support, and his efforts to give back by working within the correctional system to inspire others who are facing similar battles.


Ricky’s story highlights the significance of faith, resilience, and the importance of having a support system. He emphasizes that no matter how deep the darkness, there is always a way back through positive mindset, hard work, and faith in a higher power. His message is especially impactful for those struggling with addiction, incarceration, or family members who want to support loved ones on their path to recovery and redemption. His journey from darkness to light serves as a beacon of hope for anyone striving to rewrite their story.


Join us as we explore how one man’s determination to change not only transformed his own life but also opened doors for him to help others through motivational speaking, prison outreach, and community service. Ricky’s story is a reminder that our past does not define our future and that with faith, effort, and perseverance, everyone has the power to live louder and better than ever before.

episodes.description_html:
Join us on the Living Louder podcast as we delve into powerful stories of resilience, redemption, and transformation. In this episode, Sheri bravely shares her extraordinary journey from a childhood filled with trauma, addiction, and incarceration to finding hope and sobriety. Her story highlights the harsh realities faced by many who grow up in environments plagued by violence, substance abuse, and systemic challenges, yet also demonstrates the potential for healing and renewal through perseverance and support.


Sheri's narrative takes us through her tumultuous youth, including her experiences with foster placements, juvenile detention, and life on the streets. She recounts her time in various correctional programs and her struggles with addiction, highlighting how her environment shaped her decisions and mindset. Her story is a testament to the power of hope and the human capacity to change, even after hitting rock bottom, inspiring others to believe in their own potential for a better life.


This episode also explores themes of family, love, and resilience. Sheri reflects on her relationships with her children, her sisters, and the support systems that helped her turn her life around. Her journey underscores the importance of connection, understanding, and compassion in overcoming life's most difficult challenges. Tune in to hear Sheri's compelling story of survival and redemption. Her resilience serves as a powerful reminder that despite life's hardships, change is possible, and everyone has the strength to create a new path. episodes.title: Ride or Die Friend - Lisa Bearnson
episodes.description_html:
Welcome to the Living Louder podcast, where stories of resilience, faith, and transformation take center stage. In this heartfelt episode, host Portia is joined by her lifelong friend and sister-in-spirit, Lisa Bernson, for a candid and inspiring conversation about life's greatest challenges and the power of authentic connection. From their serendipitous meeting in a church ward to navigating the complexities of incarceration, addiction, and personal growth, Lisa and Portia share their journey of healing, forgiveness, and the unbreakable bonds of friendship.


Throughout the episode, Lisa and Portia reflect on the profound ways in which love and support can transform lives. Lisa recounts her experience visiting Portia in prison, emphasizing the importance of compassion, listening, and being present during life's most difficult moments. Their stories highlight the significance of owning one's mistakes, seeking divine guidance, and embracing a path of continuous growth. Their conversations serve as a reminder that no matter how dark the night, there is always a way back to hope, purpose, and peace.


In addition to their personal stories, the episode explores the everyday habits and simple acts that create lasting positive change. From daily routines like prayer and gratitude to the therapeutic joy of finding golf balls at night, Lisa shares how small, consistent actions can lead to profound transformation. The duo also discusses their shared commitment to community service, faith-based living, and supporting others in overcoming adversity. Their authentic dialogue encourages listeners to reflect on their own journeys and to remember that everyone has the capacity for renewal and redemption.


Lisa’s adventurous spirit shines through as she recounts her unique hobby of collecting and finding golf balls, which she describes as both therapeutic and meaningful. Meanwhile, Portia opens up about her emotional journey of returning home from prison, the humility she gained, and her resolve to rebuild her life grounded in faith and integrity. Together, they celebrate the beauty of second chances and the importance of owning one’s story with honesty and grace. Their conversation is a testament to the resilience of the human spirit and the transformative power of love.


Join us for an uplifting episode filled with raw honesty, heartfelt friendship, and inspiring messages of hope. Whether you're facing your own struggles or simply seeking encouragement to live louder and truer, this conversation reminds us all that lives can be changed for good. episodes.title: There's Got To Be More To Life Than This - Ed McGarr
episodes.description_html:
Join us for an inspiring and heartfelt episode of the Living Louder podcast, where faith, redemption, and personal transformation take center stage. In this conversation, Ed shares his remarkable journey from a challenging childhood in Queens, New York, through years of addiction, reckless behavior, and feeling lost in life. His story takes a powerful turn when missionaries knock on his door, introducing him to the gospel of Jesus Christ. Ed’s experience of spiritual awakening and the life-changing moment when he prays and feels the Holy Spirit testify to him is a testament to the profound power of faith and divine intervention.

Throughout the episode, Ed emphasizes the importance of understanding our divine nature and the eternal perspective that religion and spirituality can offer. He discusses how his life was transformed by embracing Christ’s teachings, repentance, and service in the church, including his time as a bishop in Queens and his missionary service in San Diego. Ed also touches on how embracing diversity, love, and acceptance is at the core of his faith, regardless of past mistakes or societal labels. His message encourages everyone to see beyond their flaws and past sins, understanding that change and growth are always possible.

The conversation delves into the significance of personal development, meditation, and scripture study as tools for connecting with God and finding inner peace. Ed shares how practices like transcendental meditation, combined with prayer and scripture, have helped him navigate life's challenges and foster a deeper relationship with the divine. His insights highlight that true happiness comes from knowing who we are as children of God and loving others unconditionally. Whether you're religious or simply seeking inspiration, this episode offers valuable lessons on hope, resilience, and the transformative power of faith.

Tune in to hear these powerful stories, practical advice, and spiritual insights that remind us all of our divine potential. Ed’s journey from darkness to light serves as a beacon of hope for anyone struggling with their past or searching for meaning. Remember, no matter where you come from or what you've been through, change is always within reach, and you are loved beyond measure. Don’t miss this uplifting episode of Living Louder, and join us as we celebrate the eternal truth that we are all divine and connected through the love of Jesus Christ.
